newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan and PLO coordinate over Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Jordan and PLO coordinate over Jerusalem.

text.p: Jordan and the Palestinian Authority began talks on Sunday to coordinate efforts to preserve Moslem holy sites in Arab East Jerusalem from Israeli designs, a senior Palestinian official said.

"The meeting is part of the coordination between the Palestinian Authority and Jordan that is for the good of the city of Jerusalem and Islamic holy sites against Israeli designs," Hassan Tahboub, in charge of the religious affairs portfolio in the Palestinian Authority (PA), told Reuters.

Officials said talks between Jordan's Religious Affairs Minister Abdul Salam al-Abbadi and the Palestinian delegation headed by Tahboub were the first to focus on the thorny issue of the Moslem holy sites in Arab East Jerusalem.
Jordan and the Palestinian Authority in charge of self-rule territories are enjoying their warmest ties in many years.

Tensions have traditionally run deep over a historic dispute over who should represent the Palestinian people and control over Jerusalem's holy sites. Jordan ruled over the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, from 1950 until its capture by Israel in the 1967 War.
Heightened worries that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies endanger the future of the Middle East peace process are drawing the PLO and Jordan closer.
Jordan accused Israel of violating the sanctity of Jerusalem and provoking Moslems around the world by opening last September a tunnel beside the al-Aqsa Mosque -- the third holiest Moslem shrine.

King Hussein, playing a custodianship role over the holy city's Moslem sites, was personally angered by Israel's move which he considered a violation of the 1994 Jordan-Israel treaty. The treaty recognised Amman's "special role" over Moslem holy shrines in Arab Jerusalem -- a thorn in Jordanian-PLO ties.

The tunnel incident, which fuelled the worst wave of violence since the 1993 Israel-PLO Oslo accords, strained the normally warm relations between Jordan and Israel. The ties with Jordan have been the warmest Israel has had with any Arab state.

Tahboub said the talks will cover the existing status and upkeep of the Moslem sites in Arab East Jerusalem and means to cover an undisclosed shortfall in the upkeep. He said he hoped a follow-up committee would be set up to boost coordination.
Jordan still maintains the salaries of Palestinian employees working in the al-Aqsa Mosque complex.
